core_obligations: Produce an injective ring map: by the local-Noetherian hypothesis one finds an affine open neighbourhood U of x such that R = O_X(U) -> O_{X,x} is injective (proof lines 610-613).
Translate the hypothesis: by the point-wise characterisation, geometric reducedness of X at x means that the local ring O_{X,x} is geometrically reduced over k (proof lines 614-616).

Conclude for the neighbourhood: the subalgebra criterion for geometric reducedness applies to the injection R -> O_{X,x}, so R is geometrically reduced over k, and therefore its spectrum U is geometrically reduced over k (proof lines 617-619).
proof_roadmap: Choose an affine open U around x with O_X(U) -> O_{X,x} injective, using local Noetherianity (proof lines 610-613).
Reinterpret the hypothesis as geometric reducedness of the local ring (proof lines 614-616).
Apply the subalgebra criterion to R and read the conclusion off on U (proof lines 617-619).
difficulty_reason: The lemma passes from a point-wise hypothesis to an open neighbourhood: for a locally Noetherian scheme X over k that is geometrically reduced at a point x, there is an open neighbourhood U of x which is geometrically reduced over k (statement lines 600-605). The proof has three separate inputs in a fixed order: local Noetherianity produces an affine open U whose ring injects into the local ring O_{X,x}, the point-wise characterisation turns the hypothesis into geometric reducedness of that local ring, and the subalgebra criterion then descends geometric reducedness to the subring R = O_X(U) (proof lines 610-619). The step that is not automatic is the middle one, since the hypothesis is about a point while the conclusion is about a neighbourhood. The claim is H2.
